description: A session-only planar Earth orbit workbench for learning and executing a two-impulse transfer: choose a starting orbit, preview local tangential/radial burns, coast to apsides, and circularize against an adjustable target. Includes live orbit plotting, current/proposed orbit comparison, mission telemetry, time acceleration, flight log, recoverable burns/coasts/resets, collision handling, and in-product physics help.

numericalAssumptions: Earth-centered, inertial, planar Newtonian two-body motion with Earth gravitational parameter 398600.4418 km^3/s^2 and spherical radius 6371 km.
Massless spacecraft; no backreaction. RK4 propagation with dt <= 10 seconds and dt <= local gravitational timescale / 100.
Burns are instantaneous in the local radial/tangential frame. Tangential positive follows orbital angular momentum sign, rather than velocity direction for eccentric motion.
Apsis coasting times use elliptic Kepler elements, then propagate the actual state using RK4.
Orbit lines use osculating conics; target completion is both apsides within 25 km and eccentricity below 0.01.
limitations: No atmosphere, drag, oblateness, perturbing bodies, inclination, fuel use, finite burn duration, or uncertainty. Not suitable for navigation.
Collision detection is performed at integration step endpoints and can stop up to one step after surface crossing.
Apsis coast action is bounded to seven days and unavailable for circular or unbound orbits; continuous propagation remains available.
Escape conics and very large orbits are clipped to a bounded view. Earth-close-up may place spacecraft outside view.
Flight state is session-only. Undo restores only the state before the most recent burn, coast, or reset; it is not a full timeline rewind.
Animation clamps wall-time elapsed per frame to 0.1 seconds, so background tabs do not catch up to elapsed real time.
